title: CPU Image Captioning: Service Health to Hardware
description: A4 observability dashboard: Streamlit BLIP captioning app + node_exporter.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content:
**CPU image-captioning service.** Read top to bottom: **1 Health** (is it up?) → **2 Traffic** (how much work?) → **3 Latency** (how fast?) → **4 Workload** (what is the app doing internally?) → **5 System** (what does it cost the machine?).  
Colours are colour-blind safe and fixed: **blue = single-image mode / healthy**, **orange = bulk (ZIP) mode**, red only for problems (always with text). Shaded regions on time-series panels mark **running bulk jobs**, so app spikes can be matched to CPU/RAM spikes in section 5. Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it shows. All panels refresh every 5 s.

panels.title: 1 · Health: is everything up?
Caption app
panels.description: Is Prometheus able to scrape the app's /metrics endpoint (port 8000)? UP = app process alive.

panels.title: node_exporter
panels.description: Is the host metrics exporter (port 9100) reachable? Needed for section 5.

panels.title: Model loaded
panels.description: 1 when the captioning model has finished loading into memory and can serve requests.

panels.title: App uptime
panels.description: Time since the Streamlit app process started.

panels.title: Active sessions (5 min)
panels.description: Distinct browser sessions that interacted with the app in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Image error rate (5 min)
panels.description: Share of images that failed (unreadable file, model error) over the last 5 minutes. Red above 5 %.

panels.title: 2 · Traffic: how much work is arriving?
Requests per minute, by mode (linear)
panels.description: How many caption requests users start. A bulk request is one whole ZIP. Spikes = users uploading.

panels.title: Images captioned per second, by outcome (linear)
panels.description: Model throughput. 'success' should track uploads; any 'error' line means files were rejected or failed.

panels.title: Errors by type, per minute (linear)
panels.description: What is going wrong: invalid_image, unsupported_file, zip_corrupt, zip_too_large, inference_error...

panels.title: Requests by client (session · IP · browser)
panels.description: Who is using the app. Each row is one browser session, from the custom labels on caption_client_requests_total.

panels.title: 3 · Latency: how fast is each caption?
Model inference time per image: p50 / p95 / p99 (seconds, linear)
panels.description: From the caption_inference_seconds histogram. p95 = 95 % of images finish faster than this line. A rising p99 with flat p50 means occasional slow images.

panels.title: Average end-to-end request time, by mode (seconds, LOG scale)
panels.description: From the caption_request_duration_seconds summary (_sum / _count). Single = one image, bulk = a whole ZIP, so they differ by orders of magnitude, hence the log10 axis.

panels.title: Inference time distribution over time (seconds, bucketed)
panels.description: Each column is one minute; darker cells = more images finished in that latency bucket. Shows the whole distribution, not just percentiles.

panels.title: Waiting + preprocessing time per image, p95 (seconds, linear)
panels.description: Queue wait = time an image waited for the single CPU model slot (grows when users overlap). Preprocess = decode + resize. Both should stay far below inference time.

panels.title: 4 · Workload: what is the app doing right now?
Bulk queue and in-flight requests (count, linear)
panels.description: Images still waiting in running ZIP jobs, plus requests currently being processed. Use this panel to line up bulk uploads with the CPU / RAM panels directly below in section 5.

panels.title: Upload volume, by mode (bytes per second, linear)
panels.description: How much data users push into the app. Large ZIPs show up as tall orange spikes.

panels.title: Caption length and image size (averages, linear)
panels.description: Average words per caption and average uploaded image size, from the caption_text_length_words and caption_image_megapixels histograms (_sum / _count). Checks the model output stays sensible.

panels.title: Images processed (total since start)
panels.description: Lifetime count of images captioned, split by mode.

panels.title: Bulk jobs (total since start)
panels.description: ZIP jobs by outcome: completed, completed_with_errors, rejected.

panels.title: 5 · System (node_exporter): what does it cost the machine?
CPU usage: whole machine vs caption app (% of all cores, linear)
panels.description: Blue = total host CPU from node_exporter; orange = share used by the Streamlit app process. When a bulk job runs (shaded), both should rise together; the gap is everything else on the machine.

panels.title: Memory: host used vs caption app RSS (bytes, linear)
panels.description: Host used = total minus available RAM. App RSS = memory held by the app (mostly the model). Bulk jobs should NOT make RSS grow steadily; if they do, something leaks.

panels.title: Load average, 1 / 5 / 15 min (runnable tasks, linear)
panels.description: Average number of tasks wanting CPU. Above the core count means the machine is overloaded.

panels.title: Disk throughput, read vs write (bytes per second, linear)
panels.description: Disk I/O from node_exporter. Model loading and ZIP extraction cause short read bursts.

panels.title: Network traffic, receive vs transmit (bytes per second, linear)
panels.description: Host network excluding loopback. Uploads from other devices on the network appear as receive spikes.

panels.title: Root disk used (%)
panels.description: How full the main disk is. Orange above 80 %, red above 90 %.

panels.title: Caption app threads and open files (count, linear)
panels.description: Python process internals from prometheus_client's process collector. Steady values = no leaks.
